[Image: Semicircle k with diameter AB, inscribed triangle ABC, and incircle with center S]

AB is the diameter of a semicircle k, C is an arbitrary point on the semicircle (other than A or B), and S is the centre of the circle inscribed into Δ ABC.

Then the measure of

options.label: A
options.text: ∠ASB changes as C moves on k.

options.label: B
options.text: ∠ASB is the same for all positions of C but it cannot be determined without knowing the radius.

figure_description: A semicircle labeled k has a horizontal diameter AB as its base, with endpoint A on the left and endpoint B on the right. Point C lies on the arc of semicircle k, positioned toward the upper left so that AC is shorter than BC. Line segments AB, BC, and CA form triangle ABC inscribed in the semicircle, drawn with bold lines. Inside triangle ABC, a circle is inscribed such that it is tangent to all three sides of the triangle. The center of this incircle is marked with a dot labeled S.
